content_html_sanitized:
From A Reader

"While reading the Federal Times piece about workplace drug testing I noticed there were some figures not mentioned.
See Officials Involved In Workplace Drug Testing Get A Chilling Reminder Of The Hazards Of False Readings

Of 111 agencies that reported drug-testing results between April and September 1995, some 49 agencies conducted 44,193 tests. Of those, 342, about .8%, had positive use readings, HHS documents say. Of those who tested positive, 199, or 58%, were for marijuana; 96, or 28%, were for cocaine; 37,or 11% were for amphetamines. Opiates and PCP showed up eight times each. The six-month reporting period in 1995 cost $4.9 million, or about $56 per person tested, HHS documents say.

By my calculation, the ‘per person tested’ figure is actually a little over $110 each. The more revealing number I think is when you divide the cost, $4.9 million, by the number of successful (positive) results, 342, which gives you $14,327, the cost ‘per positive test’. You shouldn’t count your misses, just your hits, or kills.

They spent $2,851,073 just to detect and reject 199 people with more than 15 nanograms of THC metabolites in their urine. Another $1,375,392 per cocaine user, etc. Apparently a few were even ‘multiple’ positives. Maybe even a dozen false positives. That they don’t mention.

What a colossal waste! This from government agencies bound by the Constitution. Meanwhile the private corporations act as de facto drug law enforcers and tax collectors for the government as well. I continually wonder how these people morally, legally, or economically justify their demand of a biological sample to prove you’re qualified for a job. Do they not teach cost/benefit analysis anymore? Don’t forget to factor in the loss of employee trust.

Urinalysis is indeed an expensive habit. They must be in denial."
